## DataQ — current state (2026-07-24)

**Shipped:** v1.0.0 tagged 2026-07-04, deployed and live on Azure Container Apps. Working tree clean on `main` at `1d83463d`.

**Cycle:** v1.1 (2026-07-04 → 08-15, + W7 stretch to 08-22).

| Week | Status |
|---|---|
| W1 — Snowflake close-out + PATs | ✅ closed |
| W2 — portability (OTel logs, secrets lifecycle, dry-run depth) | ✅ closed 14/14 |
| W3 — Azure wind-down + local-first | ✅ closed 2026-07-19, 23/23 |
| W4 — `schema_drift` + flat-file monitors + DQ dimensions | ✅ closed 2026-07-19, 8/8 |
| **W5 — `anomaly` kind + metric trends (due 08-08)** | **0/8 — current, not started** |
| W6 — scale-aware execution + hardening + cycle close (08-15) | 0/14 |
| W7 — stretch backlog burn-down (08-22) | 0/10 |

**Last work landed (W4, deployed + live-verified 2026-07-19):** ADR 0038 DQ-dimension classification (#945), shared `services/rollup.py` (#948), asset DQ scorecard (#950), flat-file CSV delimiter sniffing (#934) + flat-file freshness/volume incl. arrival-time (#940), dialect-quoted monitor SQL (#937), dimension backfill (#952), and a live-only UC freshness fix (#953 — the Databricks driver returns MAX(timestamp) as a `str`; no fixture could catch it).

**W5 next up:** [#593](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/593) anomaly kind (rolling z-score over `metric_value`, `skip` on cold start) + [#594](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/594) trend view, plus a results/connections UX batch (#345/#283/#351/#424/#349) and #568 threshold-ordering validation.

**Two things worth your attention now:**
1. **Azure wind-down was planned for ~2026-07-25 — that's tomorrow.** The subscription is PayAsYouGo with no spending limit, so awake resources are billing real money.
2. [#954](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/954) — two prod Snowflake PATs are dead, and a *datasource* connection with a dead credential shows no visible state until a run fails (#839's health signal only covers orchestration connections).

No blockers otherwise; all open items are follow-ups scheduled into W5–W7.

content.text:
Triaged all 12 open PRs (all Dependabot, opened 2026-07-20) and all 6 open CodeQL alerts.

## Open PRs — 8 mergeable now, 4 blocked

**✅ Green, safe to merge (8):**

| PR | Bump |
|---|---|
| #967 | `@fontsource/inter` 5.2.8 → 5.3.0 |
| #965 | `typescript-eslint` 8.63 → 8.64 |
| #964 | `@eslint/js` 9.39.4 → 9.39.5 |
| #963 | `snowflake-connector-python` 4.6.0 → 4.7.1 |
| #962 | `snowflake-sqlalchemy` 1.10.2 → 1.11.0 |
| #961 | `@types/node` 26.0.0 → 26.1.1 |
| #957 | `actions/setup-python` 6 → 7 |
| #956 | `actions/setup-node` 6 → 7 |

(#957's only non-success is `deploy=SKIPPED`, which is correct — deploy is `workflow_dispatch`.)

**🔴 Blocked — each needs a human commit, none is a retry-and-it-passes:**

- **#958 `fastapi` 0.138.2→0.139.2** and **#959 `fastmcp` 3.4.3→3.4.4** — both fail `Backend — lint & format` with `ERROR: drift between backend/requirements-typecheck.txt and .pre-commit-config.yaml mypy hook deps`. Dependabot only edits [requirements.txt](backend/requirements.txt); the same pins are re-listed at [requirements-typecheck.txt:16](backend/requirements-typecheck.txt#L16) / [:18](backend/requirements-typecheck.txt#L18) and [.pre-commit-config.yaml:25](.pre-commit-config.yaml#L25) / [:27](.pre-commit-config.yaml#L27). Fix = a two-line fixup commit on each branch mirroring the version. This is structural: **every** Dependabot bump of a typecheck-listed package will fail this way.

- **#960 `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http` 1.43.0→1.44.0** — `ResolutionImpossible`. The exporter is pinned alongside `opentelemetry-sdk==1.43.0` ([requirements.txt:40-44](backend/requirements.txt#L40-L44)) and 1.44.0 requires SDK 1.44. Needs a coordinated bump of `opentelemetry-sdk` + the two `opentelemetry-instrumentation-*` `0.64b0` pins together. The pip-audit job burned 4 retries on it because the retry loop treats install failure as a transient PyPI 5xx — it isn't.

- **#966 `monaco-editor` 0.55.1→0.56.0** — **a real breaking change, not a flake.** 618 tests pass; the suite fails to even load because `monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/editor.worker?worker` no longer resolves — 0.56 changed the worker entry path. [SqlEditorField.tsx:3](frontend/src/components/checks/SqlEditorField.tsx#L3) needs updating to the new subpath, and since this is the Monaco custom-SQL editor (ADR 0019), it wants a live check in the browser, not just green CI.

**Systemic fix worth one PR:** `.github/dependabot.yml` has **no `groups:` config** — that's why the OTel bump arrived alone and un-mergeable. Adding an `opentelemetry` group (and one for the frontend dev-tooling churn) would collapse most of this recurring noise.

## CodeQL — 6 open, all `note`, zero with a security severity

| # | Rule | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 61 | `py/unused-global-variable` — `COMPARISON_KIND` | **False positive.** It's imported and used in 8 modules ([check_service.py:72](backend/app/services/check_service.py#L72), [run_service.py:141](backend/app/services/run_service.py#L141), `comparison_run.py`, `suite_io_service.py`, `runs.py`). The query only sees module-local reads. Dismiss as *false positive*. |
| 52, 53, 57, 58 | `py/cyclic-import` in `backend/app/lineage/` | **By design.** [warehouse.py:170-184](backend/app/lineage/warehouse.py#L170-L184) lazy-imports the two providers inside `get_warehouse_lineage_provider()` specifically so the module stays free of the SQLAlchemy-heavy impls — the docstring says so. The cycle never exists at import time. Dismiss as *won't fix*, with that note. |
| 56 | `py/unnecessary-lambda` in [test_warehouse_lineage_task.py:60](backend/tests/worker/test_warehouse_lineage_task.py#L60) | **Real but cosmetic**, in test code. One-line cleanup or dismiss. |

Also open: **1 Dependabot alert** — `dompurify` `CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING` bypass, severity **low**, no fix PR raised.

**Suggested order:** merge the 8 green ones → one PR that adds Dependabot groups + fixes the typecheck-sync drift for #958/#959 → handle the OTel group bump → treat #966 as a small task with a browser check. Want me to start on any of these? The dismissals need to go through the GitHub API, which changes repo state, so I'll ask before firing those.

GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (**high**) — *React Router: RSC Mode CSRF Bypass Allows Action Execution Before 400 Response* — matches our resolved \`react-router@7.18.1\`. The advisory's vulnerable range is \`>=7.12.0, <8.3.0\` and **the only patched version is 8.3.0**, i.e. a major-version bump from our \`react-router-dom@^7.18.1\`.

## Why it is not exploitable today

The bypass is specific to React Router's **RSC (React Server Components) mode**. DataQ is a Vite SPA that mounts the router declaratively via \`<BrowserRouter>\` (\`frontend/src/main.tsx:47\`) — we do not use RSC mode, server actions, or the \`unstable_\` RSC entry points. The vulnerable code path is unreachable.

## Current state

Because \`scripts/audit_bulk.cjs\` is a blocking merge gate at \`--audit-level=high\`, this advisory red-lined **every** open PR (including Python-only ones). It is currently waived by a documented, package-scoped entry in that script's \`ALLOWLIST\`, added alongside the js-yaml / brace-expansion override bumps.

## What to do here

1. Upgrade \`react-router-dom\` to \`^8.3.0\` and work through the v8 breaking changes.
2. Full UI regression pass — every route, the nav shell, deep links, and the 404/403 error pages.
3. **Delete the \`GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2\` entry from \`ALLOWLIST\` in \`frontend/scripts/audit_bulk.cjs\`.** The script fails closed on a stale allowlist entry, so leaving it in place after the upgrade will break CI by design — that is the intended forcing function.

## Notes

Deliberately scheduled rather than done inline: a router major is real migration work with UI-wide blast radius, not a lockfile bump." 2>&1 | tail -3

GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (**high**) — *brace-expansion: DoS via unbounded expansion length causing an out-of-memory process crash* — declares its vulnerable range as \`<= 5.0.7\` with **5.0.8 as the only patched version**. Semver-wise that range swallows the entire 1.x and 2.x lines, so \`brace-expansion@1.1.16\` (the newest 1.x, which does clear the *other* advisory GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp) still matches.

## Why we cannot just take 5.0.8 everywhere

Tried and verified broken. Forcing a flat \`\"brace-expansion\": \">=5.0.8\"\` override makes \`pnpm lint\` die with:

\`\`\`
TypeError: expand is not a function
    at Minimatch.braceExpand (node_modules/.pnpm/minimatch@3.1.5/node_modules/minimatch/minimatch.js:271:10)
\`\`\`

\`minimatch@3.1.5\` declares \`brace-expansion: ^1.1.7\` and consumes the **default** export; brace-expansion 5 removed it. The 1.x line has no release above 1.1.16, so there is no in-line fix.

## Why it is acceptable today

\`minimatch@3\` reaches us only through **dev-only lint tooling** — \`eslint@9\`, \`@eslint/config-array\`, \`eslint-plugin-react\`. It is never bundled into the SPA and never runs in production. The only glob patterns it expands are the ones we write ourselves in \`eslint.config.js\`; no attacker-controlled input reaches it, so the OOM DoS has no reachable trigger.

The 5.x line in our graph **is** on the patched 5.0.8 (via \`minimatch@10\`) — only the 1.x branch is waived, and the waiver is version-scoped to \`1.x\` so a future vulnerable 5.x would still fail the gate.

When eslint's transitive \`minimatch@3\` disappears (an eslint/config-array upgrade that moves to \`minimatch@10\`), the \`brace-expansion@1\` override and the \`GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg\` \`ALLOWLIST\` entry in \`frontend/scripts/audit_bulk.cjs\` both become dead weight.

The script **fails closed on a stale allowlist entry**, so it will tell you when that day arrives — CI will demand the entry's removal. No polling needed.

| Package | Requires |
|---|---|
| \`opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.44.0\` | \`opentelemetry-sdk~=1.44.0\` (i.e. \`>=1.44.0,<1.45\`) |
| \`azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter==1.0.0b55\` | \`opentelemetry-sdk~=1.43.0\` (i.e. \`>=1.43.0,<1.44\`) |

\`1.0.0b55\` is the **latest** release of the Azure exporter, so there is no version of it today that accepts SDK 1.44. #960 was closed as upstream-blocked rather than left red.

## What to do when unblocked

Watch for an \`azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter\` release that widens its SDK pin to \`~=1.44\`, then bump the whole stack **as one commit** — these versions move in lockstep and bumping any one alone reproduces the same conflict:

- \`opentelemetry-sdk\` 1.43.0 → 1.44.0
- \`opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http\` 1.43.0 → 1.44.0
- \`opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi\` 0.64b0 → 0.65b0
- \`opentelemetry-instrumentation-celery\` 0.64b0 → 0.65b0
- \`azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter\` 1.0.0b55 → whatever ships the widened pin

(The \`0.6Nb0\` instrumentation line tracks the \`1.N\` core line — 0.65b0 pairs with 1.44.)

## Follow-up worth doing regardless

\`.github/dependabot.yml\` has **no \`groups:\` config**, which is why this arrived as a lone un-mergeable PR. An \`opentelemetry\` group would make Dependabot raise the five bumps together and this class of conflict would stop recurring.

Also noted: the \`pip-audit\` CI step burned all 4 of its retries on this, because the retry loop treats any install failure as a transient PyPI/OSV 5xx. A resolution conflict is deterministic and should fail fast." 2>&1 | tail -2

### Dependency & CodeQL triage (2026-07-24)

A full sweep of the 12 open Dependabot PRs + 6 open CodeQL alerts. **11 of 12 PRs merged**; the twelfth is closed as upstream-blocked.

Four of the twelve were not retry-able flakes, and the shape is worth remembering — **a red Dependabot PR is a signal, not noise**:

| PR | Looked like | Actually was |
|---|---|---|
| #958 / #959 (fastapi, fastmcp) | lint failure | Dependabot updates `requirements.txt` **and** `requirements-typecheck.txt`, but never `.pre-commit-config.yaml`'s mypy hook deps — the third place the same pins live. `typecheck-deps-sync` catches it every time. **Structural: any bump of a typecheck-listed package fails this way.** |
| #960 (otel exporter) | `ResolutionImpossible` | `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.44.0` needs `sdk~=1.44`; `azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter==1.0.0b55` (**latest**) needs `sdk~=1.43`. No intersection, no version of the Azure exporter accepts 1.44 → **closed, tracked in #970**. The `pip-audit` step burned all 4 retries on it because the loop treats any install failure as a transient PyPI 5xx; a resolution conflict is deterministic. |
| #966 (monaco 0.56) | test flake (618 passing) | 0.56 added an `exports` map (`"./*.js": "./esm/vs/*.js"`), making `esm/vs/` implicit — the old deep worker specifier stopped resolving, so the whole test file failed to **load**. Fixed to `monaco-editor/editor/editor.worker.js?worker`; build re-verified to still emit the worker chunk. |

**Mid-sweep, three advisories published 2026-07-24 red-lined `pnpm audit` on `main`**, so every open PR failed the gate — including Python-only #963. Fixed in [#971](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/971): js-yaml → 4.3.0, brace-expansion → 1.1.16 / 5.0.8 (**bounded** overrides — an open-ended `>=4.3.0` let pnpm jump js-yaml to the 5.x major), plus a **version-scoped allowlist** for the two with no reachable fix (#968 react-router, #969 brace-expansion 1.x). The allowlist treats a **stale entry as a hard `exit 2`**, so CI demands each waiver's deletion once the dependency moves on — that is what makes #968/#969 self-closing instead of forgotten.

Two things only checking could have told me, both recorded because guessing would have gone the other way: forcing brace-expansion 5 everywhere **breaks lint outright** (`minimatch@3` declares `^1.1.7` and calls the default export v5 dropped — `TypeError: expand is not a function`), and monaco's 0.56 worker file **still exists**; only the path to reach it changed. Both new allowlist guards were **mutation-checked** before being trusted.

**CodeQL: 6 open → 0.** Only one was a real finding (#56, `py/unnecessary-lambda` in a test — fixed in [#972](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/972)). The other five were dismissed with reasons recorded on each alert: #52/#53/#57/#58 (`py/cyclic-import` in `lineage/`) are the **deliberate** lazy-import registry in `warehouse.py:170-184` — no cycle exists at import time; #61 (`COMPARISON_KIND` unused) is a false positive, the constant is used across 8 modules and the query only sees module-local reads.

Noted, not filed (pre-existing, unrelated to the bumps): the frontend build emits **five** Monaco worker chunks — `ts.worker` alone is 6.9 MB — though `SqlEditorField.tsx` documents that only the base editor worker is needed. Verified identical on 0.55.1, so it is not a 0.56 regression; `import * as monaco from 'monaco-editor'` pulls every language service. Lazily loaded, so no runtime cost, but ~9 MB of dead artifacts ship each deploy.

### Pending design decisions

**A passing verification confirms the world's state, not your story about why.**
Before claiming a change fixed something, prove the change *caused* the fix —
check the baseline without it.

**Where this bit (2026-07-24, PR #974):** I bumped a `dompurify` pnpm override
from `>=3.4.11` to `>=3.4.12` to close a Dependabot alert, then "verified" it by

transitively. My lockfile diff contained **only the `overrides:` header line**;
no resolved version changed. The alert then auto-closed as `fixed` on its own.

The commit message therefore described a bump that never happened and credited
the PR for another PR's effect. The tell was visible the whole time and I did
not read it: **a dependency "bump" whose lockfile diff shows no resolution
change did not bump anything.**

**How to apply:**
- When a fix's verification passes, ask "would this have passed *without* my
  change?" For dependency work that is one command:
  `git show origin/main:<lockfile> | grep <pkg>`.
- Treat a no-op lockfile diff as a red flag on any commit claiming a version bump.
- This matters most in a security context: an overrides block is an artifact
  people audit later for *why* each bound exists. A bound justified by a
  high-sounding advisory that was actually low and already fixed is the same
  stale-rationale rot that `frontend/scripts/audit_bulk.cjs` deliberately guards
  against in its `ALLOWLIST`.

Keeping the change was still right (it ratchets the floor and adds the missing
`<4` ceiling) — the defect was the *stated reason*, and the fix was rewording,
not reverting. Caught by the `/code-review` agent pass, which is why
[[feedback_agents_allowed_without_asking]] earns its keep. Same family as
[[feedback_test_failure_modes]]: "passes" is not "passes for the right reason."

cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; gh issue create --title "Frontend bundle ships ~9 MB of unused Monaco language-service workers" --label "enhancement,priority/P3" --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" --body "## What

Every production build emits **five** Monaco worker chunks, four of which the app has no use for:

| Chunk | Size |
|---|---|
| \`ts.worker\` | **6.9 MB** |
| \`css.worker\` | 1.1 MB |
| \`html.worker\` | 740 kB |
| \`json.worker\` | 430 kB |
| \`editor.worker\` | 300 kB ← the only one we need |

This directly contradicts what the component documents. [\`frontend/src/components/checks/SqlEditorField.tsx\`](../blob/main/frontend/src/components/checks/SqlEditorField.tsx):

> Monaco is bundled locally (not fetched from a CDN) so the app stays self-contained and CSP-friendly. **SQL is a basic (highlight-only) language, so only the base editor worker is needed — no language-service worker.**

The intent is right; the bundle does not match it.

## Cause

\`import * as monaco from 'monaco-editor'\` pulls the full \`editor.main\` surface, which registers every bundled language contribution, so Vite emits a worker chunk per language service. \`self.MonacoEnvironment.getWorker\` only ever returns \`editorWorker\`, so the other four are **emitted but never requested**.

## Not a regression

Verified by building both sides: monaco **0.55.1** (pre-#966) and **0.56.0** (post-#966) emit the identical five chunks at near-identical sizes. This is long-standing, not fallout from the 0.56 bump — recorded so nobody bisects for it.

## Impact

Low but not zero. The chunks are lazily loaded, so there is **no runtime cost** for users — nothing fetches them. The cost is ~9 MB of dead artifacts in every image and every deploy, and a bundle whose contents contradict its own documented intent, which misleads the next person reading it.

## Fix direction

Import the narrow entry point instead of the barrel — e.g. \`monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/editor.api\` plus only the SQL basic-language contribution — so the language services never enter the graph. Note that **0.56 changed the subpath layout**: it added an \`exports\` map (\`\"./*.js\": \"./esm/vs/*.js\"\`) that makes \`esm/vs/\` implicit, which is what broke the worker import in #966. Specifiers need to be written against the new map.

Verify by diffing \`dist/assets/\` before and after: success is \`editor.worker\` surviving alone, SQL highlighting still working in the custom-SQL check editor, and the \`monaco-*.js\` chunk shrinking from its current 4.4 MB.

Found during the 2026-07-24 dependency triage while confirming #966's worker fix actually bundled." 2>&1|tail -2

**2586 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** — 97.18% coverage, gate met.

## The two tests

Both pass. They were never broken — `test_custom_sql_gx.py` needs a live SQL backend (GX's `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` is SQL-only), and `conftest.py` builds the URL from your `.env` Postgres creds, so with the DB down it *attempts* a connection instead of skipping.

## What the exercise actually turned up

The more useful finding is how weak the earlier local runs were:

| Run | Services up | Passed | Skipped | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | none | 1642 | **943** | 0 (2 errors) |
| Postgres only | pg | 2582 | 2 | **3** |
| Both | pg + redis | **2586** | 1 | **0** |

Starting Postgres moved ~940 tests from *skipped* to *actually executing* — about a third of the backend suite had been silently not running. Then three of those newly-live tests failed for a **second** missing service: Redis backs the SecretStore, so `secret_store.set()` raised `SecretWriteError` → `ConnectionSecretWriteError`. Two layers of environmental skip, each hiding the next.

That's the same shape as the lesson already in your project notes — *a test that cannot express the failing case proves nothing*. Here the tests could express it fine; they just never ran, and the summary line said "passed" either way. A local run with the stack down reports green over a suite that is a third dark, which is exactly the failure mode the "verify locally before pushing" rule exists to prevent.

## State

- `main` clean and current; 0 open PRs, 0 CodeQL alerts, 0 Dependabot alerts.
- conda env synced — all 35 pins match, `pip check` clean, full suite green on it.
- pnpm was already current.
- `dataq-postgres-1` and `dataq-redis-1` are **still running** — I left them up since they're needed for a meaningful local test run. `docker compose down` if you want them stopped.
- Monaco worker bloat filed as [#976](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/976).

One thing I'd suggest, though I haven't done it: `scripts/test-backend.sh` presumably handles bringing the stack up, but a bare `pytest` — which is what editors and I both run — degrades to a third-coverage pass with no warning. A loud notice when `TEST_DATABASE_URL` resolves but the connection fails would turn that silent degradation into a visible one. Say the word and I'll file or implement it.

The skip *reasons* are good and actionable (\`conftest.py\` says \"start it with \`docker compose up -d postgres redis\`\"), but they are only rendered with \`-rs\`, which nobody passes by default. A skip count on its own is indistinguishable from the ~940 live-datasource tests that legitimately skip without credentials.

## Why it bites

The working agreement is to verify locally before pushing rather than lean on CI ([[feedback_verify_locally_before_push]]). A bare \`pytest\` is what editors' test runners invoke (VS Code / PyCharm call pytest directly, not \`scripts/test-backend.sh\`) — and it is what I ran. Green over a suite that is a third dark makes \"I verified locally\" mean much less than it appears to, without anyone noticing.

## It layers, which is the nastier part

Bringing up **only Postgres** does not fix it — it moves ~940 tests from *skipped* to *executing*, and then **three of them fail** against a second missing service:

\`\`\`
backend/app/services/connection_service.py:227: ConnectionSecretWriteError
[info] secret_store_initialized  backend=redis
[warning] connection_secret_write_failed  env=dev type=snowflake
\`\`\`

The SecretStore resolves to the Redis backend (via \`SECRET_STORE\` in \`.env.app\`), so \`secret_store.set()\` raises \`SecretWriteError\`. Two layers of environmental degradation, each hiding the next — and the first layer's skip concealed the second layer's failure entirely.

## What to change

Keep the skip behaviour — running the pure-unit suite anywhere is deliberate (\`conftest.py\` resolution order, point 3). Make the degradation **loud** instead of silent:

1. **\`pytest_report_header\`** — state up front whether the test Postgres and the configured SecretStore backend are reachable, so the condition is visible before the run rather than inferred after it.
2. **\`pytest_terminal_summary\`** — when infrastructure was unreachable *and* tests skipped, print a prominent warning naming what was down, how many tests it cost, and the exact command to fix it.

Probes must be cheap (short connect timeout, once per session) and must never fail the run — this is a visibility fix, not a new gate. In CI both services are up, so the header records \"reachable\" and the warning never fires.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Local test-infra visibility (#977)
#
# Skipping when the compose stack is down is deliberate (resolution order above,
# point 3) — but it must never be QUIET. With the stack down a bare `pytest -q`

#
# The per-test skip reasons are already good, but pytest only renders them under
# `-rs`, and a bare skip count is indistinguishable from the live-datasource
# tests that legitimately skip without credentials. Editors (VS Code, PyCharm)
# invoke pytest directly rather than scripts/test-backend.sh, so this is the
# common path, not an edge case.
#
# These hooks report the condition up front and again, loudly, at the end. They
# are visibility only: probes are cheap, failures are swallowed, and nothing here
# can fail a run. In CI both services are up, so the warning never fires.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S = 1.5
_FIX_HINT = "docker compose up -d postgres redis  (or scripts/test-backend.sh)"


def _probe_postgres() -> str | None:
    """None when the test DB is reachable, else a short human reason."""
    if not TEST_DATABASE_URL:
        return "no TEST_DATABASE_URL and no local .env Postgres creds"
    try:
        from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text

        engine = create_engine(
            TEST_DATABASE_URL,
            future=True,
            connect_args={"connect_timeout": int(_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S)},
        )
        try:
            with engine.connect() as conn:
                conn.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
        finally:
            engine.dispose()
    except Exception:
        return "not reachable"
    return None


def _probe_secret_store() -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """(backend_name, reason_unavailable). Only the redis backend can be *down* —
    `env` is in-process and `azure_key_vault` is never used by the local suite."""
    try:
        settings = get_settings()
        mode = settings.secret_store
    except Exception:
        return ("unknown", None)
    if mode != "redis":
        return (mode, None)
    try:
        import redis

        client = redis.Redis.from_url(
            settings.redis_url,
            socket_connect_timeout=_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S,
            socket_timeout=_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        try:
            client.ping()
        finally:
            client.close()
    except Exception:
        return (mode, "not reachable")
    return (mode, None)


def _infra_status() -> list[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """[(label, reason_unavailable)] — cached for the session."""
    global _INFRA_STATUS_CACHE
    if _INFRA_STATUS_CACHE is None:
        store_mode, store_reason = _probe_secret_store()
        _INFRA_STATUS_CACHE = [
            ("postgres (test DB)", _probe_postgres()),
            (f"secret store ({store_mode})", store_reason),
        ]
    return _INFRA_STATUS_CACHE


_INFRA_STATUS_CACHE: list[tuple[str, str | None]] | None = None


def pytest_report_header() -> list[str]:
    """State infra reachability before the run, so a degraded pass is visible
    from the first line rather than inferred from a skip count at the end."""
    lines = []
    for label, reason in _infra_status():
        lines.append(f"test infra: {label} — {'OK' if reason is None else reason.upper()}")
    if any(reason for _, reason in _infra_status()):
        lines.append(f"test infra: DEGRADED — DB-backed tests will skip. Fix: {_FIX_HINT}")
    return lines


def pytest_terminal_summary(terminalreporter: object) -> None:
    """Re-state a degraded run at the end, where the summary line is read.

    The header scrolls away on a long run; this is the part that stops a
    third-coverage pass from being mistaken for a green one.
    """
    down = [(label, reason) for label, reason in _infra_status() if reason]
    if not down:
        return
    skipped = len(terminalreporter.stats.get("skipped", []))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    write = terminalreporter.write_line  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    write("")
    write("!" * 79, red=True, bold=True)
    write("DEGRADED RUN — this suite did NOT fully execute.", red=True, bold=True)
    for label, reason in down:

    write(f"  {skipped} test(s) skipped; the DB-backed tests are among them.", red=True)
    write(f"  Fix: {_FIX_HINT}", red=True, bold=True)
    write("A pass here does not mean what a full local run means.", red=True)
    write("!" * 79, red=True, bold=True)

def pytest_report_header() -> list[str]:
    """State infra reachability up front.

    A convenience for plain `pytest`, NOT the guarantee — pytest gates header
    output on `verbosity >= 0`, so `-q` discards these lines entirely. The
    terminal-summary banner below is what actually holds under `-q`.

    for label, reason in _infra_status():
        lines.append(f"test infra: {label} — {'OK' if reason is None else reason.upper()}")
    if any(reason for _, reason in _infra_status()):
        lines.append(f"test infra: DEGRADED — see the banner at the end. Fix: {_FIX_HINT}")

input.content:
"""The degraded-run banner in conftest (#977).

These guard a piece of *diagnostic* code, which is exactly the kind that rots
unnoticed: nothing else fails when it goes wrong, so the only signal is a
person mistaking a third-coverage run for a green one — the failure this
banner exists to prevent.

Two of the three defects these lock down survived a manual four-state
walkthrough of the feature. `trylast` was missed because every hand-check
passed `--no-cov`, so the coverage table that buries the banner was never
rendered; the psycopg-only `connect_args` was missed because every hand-check
used a postgres URL. Both are cases the manual test could not express.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import backend.tests.conftest as conftest


class _FakeReporter:
    """Stands in for pytest's TerminalReporter, capturing written lines."""

    def __init__(self, **stats: list[object]) -> None:
        self.stats: dict[str, list[object]] = stats
        self.lines: list[str] = []

    def write_line(self, line: str, **_: Any) -> None:
        self.lines.append(line)


def _banner(monkeypatch: Any, status: list[tuple[str, str | None]], **stats: list[object]) -> str:
    monkeypatch.setattr(conftest, "_INFRA_STATUS_CACHE", status)
    reporter = _FakeReporter(**stats)
    conftest.pytest_terminal_summary(reporter)
    return "\n".join(reporter.lines)


# --- the banner fires only when it should ----------------------------------


def test_healthy_infra_prints_nothing(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """A quiet gate is the whole point — noise on a healthy run trains people
    to ignore it, which is how the banner would stop working."""
    out = _banner(monkeypatch, [("postgres (test DB)", None), ("secret store (env)", None)])
    assert out == ""


def test_degraded_infra_names_the_service_and_the_fix(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    out = _banner(
        monkeypatch,
        [("postgres (test DB)", "not reachable"), ("secret store (redis)", None)],
        skipped=[object()],
    )
    assert "DEGRADED RUN" in out
    assert "postgres (test DB) — not reachable" in out
    assert "docker compose up -d postgres redis" in out
    # The healthy service must not be listed as unavailable.
    assert "secret store (redis) —" not in out


# --- the banner claims only what happened ----------------------------------
#
# A missing Postgres makes tests SKIP; a missing secret store makes them FAIL.
# Reporting one as the other would be the same untrue-status defect the banner
# is meant to catch.


def test_skips_are_reported_as_skips_not_failures(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    out = _banner(
        monkeypatch,
        [("postgres (test DB)", "not reachable")],
        skipped=[object(), object()],
    )
    assert "2 test(s) skipped" in out
    assert "failed/errored" not in out


def test_failures_are_reported_as_failures_not_skips(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """Regression: an early draft printed "0 test(s) skipped" on this path."""
    out = _banner(
        monkeypatch,
        [("secret store (redis)", "not reachable")],
        failed=[object()],
        error=[object()],
    )
    assert "2 test(s) failed/errored" in out
    assert "skipped" not in out


def test_neither_skips_nor_failures_still_warns_without_inventing_counts(
    monkeypatch: Any,
) -> None:
    out = _banner(monkeypatch, [("secret store (redis)", "not reachable")])
    assert "DEGRADED RUN" in out
    assert "test(s) skipped" not in out
    assert "test(s) failed" not in out


# --- ordering: the banner must survive the coverage table ------------------


def test_terminal_summary_is_trylast() -> None:
    """Without ``trylast``, this hook runs BEFORE pytest-cov's summary and the
    banner prints above a ~140-line term-missing table — scrolling off exactly
    like the header it backs up. Verified by hand: banner at line 6, real
    summary at line 149. This is a behavioural requirement, not a style choice.
    """
    opts = getattr(conftest.pytest_terminal_summary, "pytest_impl", {})
    assert opts.get("trylast") is True


# --- the probe must not cry wolf -------------------------------------------


def test_probe_does_not_claim_unreachable_for_a_non_psycopg_driver(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """``connect_timeout`` is libpq-specific. Passing it to another driver raises
    at connect time; swallowing that into "not reachable" would report a healthy
    database as down.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(conftest, "TEST_DATABASE_URL", "sqlite://")  # in-memory, always up
    assert conftest._probe_postgres() is None


def test_probe_reports_a_genuinely_dead_postgres(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """The other half: a real postgres URL pointing nowhere must still be caught,
    so the wolf-guard above cannot silence a true alarm.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        conftest,
        "TEST_DATABASE_URL",
        "REDACTED",
    )
    assert conftest._probe_postgres() == "not reachable"


def test_probe_without_a_url_explains_itself(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(conftest, "TEST_DATABASE_URL", None)
    reason = conftest._probe_postgres()
    assert reason is not None and "TEST_DATABASE_URL" in reason
